title: Klipper copies many unnecessary mime types
line: Copying in Inkscape and similar apps no longer makes them export the object in every format they offer, so copying is fast again.
explanation: Klipper stored every image/* format offered before the PNG, plus every text/* format, by reading each one from the copying app. Apps like Inkscape and LyX offer one object in a dozen formats that they produce on demand (SVG variants, EMF, WMF, FXG, HTML, LaTeX, XAML, POV-Ray), so each copy made them run every export, which is slow and can crash them on large selections. Now Klipper keeps only the first non-PNG image format, which is the app's original, plus PNG and plain text, and skips image and text formats offered after it.

commits.message:
klipper: only keep the original image format and none of its exports

Apps like Inkscape offer a copied object in many formats and Klipper
read all of them, making the app export it to EMF, WMF, LaTeX and more
on every copy. Now only the first image format, PNG and text are kept.

BUG: 504469

media.caption: Master: one copy from an app offering Inkscape's formats makes Klipper ask for 14 of them
With the fix: the same copy asks only for plain text, PNG and the original Inkscape SVG

review.text: The diagnosis is right that UpdateDatabaseJob::updateClipboard() asks apps like Inkscape for far too many on-demand export formats, but gating all subsequent image/* and text/* formats on an order-dependent isOriginalImageSet flag (only set for a non-PNG image/* before PNG) is too brittle. It still fails whenever text/* exports precede image/* or when only image/png is offered (such as LyX from comment #4), drops valid text/html if a non-PNG image comes first, discards standard image/svg+xml in favor of vendor image/x-inkscape-svg, and still requests image/png twice on every copy (as visible in after-1.png).
changes: Replace the order-dependent isOriginalImageSet text-skipping heuristic with principled MIME-type filtering in UpdateDatabaseJob (e.g., an explicit allowlist of standard rich-text formats instead of accepting every text/* subtype such as text/xml+fxg, text/x-tex, text/xml+xaml, and text/x-povray-script), so apps without a leading non-PNG image/* (like LyX) are fixed and legitimate text/html isn't dropped based on format order.

Investigate and eliminate the duplicate image/png request shown in after-1.png (reported in comments #0 and #4), and avoid forcing expensive PNG rasterization when a lossless vector format is already being kept if feasible.

Prefer standard image formats (e.g. image/svg+xml) over vendor-specific ones (image/x-inkscape-svg) when limiting image formats, or explicitly ensure re-pasting from Klipper history into non-Inkscape apps does not regress to raster PNG.
Verify the fix against real Inkscape and LyX (not only a synthetic clipboard producer with a hardcoded format order).
